## Design

### 2026-10-28: I started by defining the project goals for this project - Witten on a good old piece of paper!

**1.9h**

I started by defining the project goals for this project - Witten on a good old piece of paper!

![Thermal Printer Setup Notes](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/360fb2a9edeb7653727e962943b57d6ebe8293720bd2f79e4dc7cb3812737587.jpg)

My core ideas include:
* A physical messaging system to connect back to a more physical connection of text.
* Stand alone capability anywhere in the world with a single usb-c port for power & programming.
* Low cost - remain within the tier 1 project budget for core components.
* Simple physical user interface with a singular button for printing & remote app? - access to change print settings and content ( maybe even send messages to other users?)
* Provide short easy to understand message to your mornings ie Weather report, Transit times, Daily quote.
* Classy case  that fits into any space.

To choose  a printer I had set myself a few requirements to meet these goals - luckily the exact thing I need does exist for around $20 which has a input voltage from 5v-9v   and uses ttl communication ( basically RX & TX) so I can hopefully use any standard usb-c cable on the esp 32. that I will use and then add a few capacitors ( a larger one near the printer  to prevent brownouts and one near the esp for good practice although I feel this might not be necessary) ![Screenshot 2026-10-28 at 22.44.41](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/05eb970479651bbff1e248e20fc782aa63cc00defd89b6f9b087f98d8d62be14.png)The printer is the GOOJPRT QR701 Mini 58mm Embedded Receipt Thermal Printer  I have seen this used before with an arduino nano so there is some reference point or communication I can look back to.

![Screenshot 2026-10-28 at 22.45.03](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/afB45WLTnSAsFqrMq92IoTER2dLA2UXI/b806bf4fe0b6720fe04aa8d3eb22d9a1b710227190c5bd2f66b3c4c77a8d0ce7.png)

For my microcontroller I most likely go with an esp32 C3 with an antenna so I can integrate my web based aspect of the project. I need to double check if I can take the 5v from the usbc or if I potentially need a different more stable source. That will be clarified by my next post which will probably be the schematic and initial work on the type design since i'm sort of excited for that part.
